title: Cohort-safelist Hybrid Rollout Engine (canary + shadow)
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Implement a policy engine and configuration primitives that enable safelist-driven hybrid rollouts: combine conservative traffic splits with live shadow probing to validate model quality before exposing broader cohorts. The engine must support cohort/safelist targeting (user segments, org tiers, IP subsets), step schedules with adaptive dwell times, multi-signal guardrails (latency p50/p95/p99, errors, quality regression against golden responses), token-cost gating, and an automatic rewind/rollback path when gates are breached. Include operator controls (pause, force-rollout, rewind-to-version), audit logs for every traffic decision, and a minimal Console UX to visualize current split/stage and probe results. Deliverables: config schema, runtime enforcement hooks (routing + mirroring), backpressure for bursty traffic, observability dashboards, and an end-to-end rollout playbook. Links: Confluence design draft, staging runbooks, and initial PRs (see links field).
technical_design: High-level approach: add a RolloutPolicy type to model-configs with fields: safelists (named cohort selectors), stages (ordered array of {percent, duration, mirror_probe:bool, dwell_adaptive:bool, gates:[]}), gate definitions (metric, threshold, window, direction, severity), and rewind-policy (immediate/gradual/hold). Runtime: policy compiler expands safelist into route predicates; router supports fractional traffic plus non-intrusive mirroring to a probe evaluator (golden comparator). Probe evaluator runs fuzzy-response checks (BLEU/embedding-similarity and token-level diffs) and reports to the policy controller which adjudicates gates and emits actions (advance/pause/rewind). Use existing KV-cache-friendly hashing to ensure cohort stickiness. Telemetry: emit per-stage telemetry tags and aggregate to a Rollouts dashboard. Implementation notes: reuse declarative canary engine primitives from ENG-5314, add a lightweight probe comparator service in the inference plane to avoid cross-region egress. Configs are JSON/YAML with a schema and validation. Operator API: POST /rollouts/{id}/actions for manual overrides; audit events stored in event-log with retention configurable.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema validated with JSON schema and unit tests
Router supports combined fractional split + mirror (no request duplication for primary path)
Probe evaluator runs in staging and computes quality deltas vs golden for 3 example safelists
Gates trigger automatic pause or rewind on simulated breach in staging runbook
Console shows active stage, percent, recent probe deltas, and provides pause/force-rewind controls
End-to-end staging rollout executed and postmortem with metrics attached
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging dry-run): deploy policy compiler and probe evaluator to staging; run 24h shadow for 10k requests. Phase 2 (canary with safelist): select two safelists (internal-support, early-adopters), mirror 5% for 24h, then step 1% -> 5% -> 20% with dwell times 30m/2h/6h. Phase 3 (wider lift): after 3 successful canaries lift to 50% with a 24h shadow across 100% traffic for quality scoring. Emergency plan: if any critical gate breaches, controller marks rollout state=PAUSED and triggers rewind according to rewind-policy; incident runbook will notify SRE and customer success.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler, route predicate generation, and JSON schema validation
Integration tests: simulated router with mirrored requests to probe evaluator; assert no increase in p99 served latency > 5%
Staging canary: run with synthetic traffic + replayed production traces; intentionally inject degraded responses to validate gates and auto-rewind
Chaos test: simulate probe evaluator outage and ensure router falls back to safe default (block new rollouts) and logs a clear error
End-to-end acceptance: QA verifies Console controls, audit logs, and operator override behavior
risks_mitigation: Risk: false positives from probe comparator causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use multi-signal majority (embeddings + token-diff + configurable heuristics) and require gate breaches across 2 consecutive windows before rewind. Risk: added tail latency from mirroring. Mitigation: mirror path is asynchronous to primary and probe evaluator processed on separate GPU pools with sampling. Risk: safety gaps for small cohorts. Mitigation: safelist minimum traffic floor and canary shadow for 24h before any percent split. All mitigations included in staging runbook.
